sentences.text: Petitioners are accused Nos.3 to 6 in C.C No.1041 of 2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Manjeri.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Manjeri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The case originated from a complaint filed by the Food Safety Officer alleging that the samples of Dalda Vanaspati collected from the accused was reported to be unsafe for human consumption by the Regional Analytical Laboratory as it contained 'Nickel' in excess of permissible limit.

At the same time, as per the report of the Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore,
second sample received for analysis contained 'Lead' in excess of the permissible limit, while the Nickel content was within limits.
This Crl.M.C is filed seeking to quash the proceedings in view of the divergent findings in the two reports.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners relied on the 2025:KER:20674 decision of this Court in Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd v. State of Kerala [2024 (6) KHC 251] to contend that the divergent findings of two laboratories is sufficient reason for this Court to quash the proceedings.

sentences.text: As held by this Court in Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd (supra), prosecution steps can be initiated only if the report of the Food Analyst Laboratory is confirmed by the Referral Laboratory.

Conversely, if the report of the Referral Laboratory and the Food Analyst Laboratory are divergent,
prosecution is not possible.
In the above judgment, rendered after detailed consideration of all provisions, learned Single Judge pointed out certain lacuna in the Rules also.
Even as on date, the lacuna exists.
Even otherwise, benefit of the divergent findings cannot be denied to the petitioner.
In the result, the Crl.M.C is allowed.
All further proceedings in C.C No.1041 of 2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Manjeri, as against the petitioners, is quashed.
